title: Training Plan Import
description: A training plan importable by AccelerometerLifting. LLMs generating plans MUST conform to this schema exactly.

exercise.description: Exercise id, snake_case (e.g. back_squat). Unknown ids create a custom exercise on import.

notes.description: Coach comment (form cues, intent). Shown to the lifter in the app with each set of this exercise.

start.description: Where the lift BEGINS, so the app knows which way the first movement of every rep goes. 'top' = starts at the top, first movement is down (squat, bench, leg curl). 'bottom' = starts at the bottom, first movement is up (press from the rack, deadlift, leg press). 'down'/'up' name that first movement directly and are equivalent. Machines of the same movement pattern genuinely differ, so declare it. Omitted: inferred from the exercise id, which is a guess.

concentric.description: Which way the CONCENTRIC (driving) phase moves. Default 'up'. Use 'down' for leg curls, lat pulldowns and pushdowns. Independent of 'start': that says which phase comes first, this says which direction the drive goes, and together they decide which tempo digit is the eccentric.

sensorInverted.description: True when the sensor moves OPPOSITE to the load the lifter drives — common on a cable machine, where the sensor rides the weight stack, so pulling the handle down sends the stack (and the sensor) up. Without this, every phase label and velocity on that exercise is backwards.

travelRatio.description: Lifter-side travel per unit of sensor travel, for pulleys that are not 1:1. A 2:1 cable moves the handle twice as far as the stack, so 2. Default 1.

prep_s.description: Seconds of prep before each set of this exercise: the pause between my starting the set and the voice guide calling the first movement, during which the app counts down and says 'Ready' then 'Brace'. Estimate THE TIME MY HANDS ARE UNAVAILABLE -- fastening straps, chalking, setting a hook grip, cinching a belt, lying down on a machine -- not the walk to the rack or loading plates, which happen before I start the set. A Romanian deadlift with straps is not ready five seconds after I tap START; a cable machine is ready in two. ONLY APPLIES TO SETS CARRYING A tempo: a set with no tempo runs no voice guide, so a prep declared on one does nothing and the app says so at the import gate. Omitted means 5. I can change it in the app, and the change comes back in the session export as prep_s beside plannedPrep_s -- author the next plan from that rather than guessing again.

optional.description: Accessory work that may be dropped when the session runs long. Surfaced in the app so the decision is planned rather than improvised.

plane.description: The plane the LIFTER moves in. 'horizontal' for seated rows, chest-press machines and horizontal cable work. This also changes how the tempo digits are read: vertical work reads them positionally (digit 1 = down stroke), while horizontal work has no up or down and reads them by phase (digit 1 = eccentric, digit 3 = concentric). Note this is the lifter's plane, not the sensor's — see sensorOnStack.

sensorOnStack.description: True when the sensor rides a cable weight stack. The stack travels VERTICALLY however the lifter moves, so a seated row measured off the stack is a vertical measurement of a horizontal exercise — set this together with plane: 'horizontal' and sensorInverted as the routing requires.

bodyweight.description: True when the lifter's own body is the load — pull-ups, dips, push-ups. The set's load_kg/load_lb is then what was ADDED, and may be NEGATIVE for band or machine assistance. Total load is the lifter's body weight (set in the app) plus that.

implementCount.description: How many IDENTICAL objects are held at once — 2 for a pair of dumbbells or a two-handled farmer's walk; 1 (the default) for a barbell, a machine, a goblet squat, a single-arm row, or one dumbbell held on a weighted dip. This does NOT change what load_kg / load_lb mean: those are ALWAYS the TOTAL across everything held. A pair of 40 lb dumbbells is "implementCount": 2 with "load_lb": 80, and the app shows it as 2 × 40 lb. Writing 40 there records half the weight lifted, and nothing afterwards can tell it apart from a real 40 lb set. It is NOT a count of limbs and must NEVER be taken from "side": a rear-foot-elevated split squat holding two dumbbells is "side": "left" WITH "implementCount": 2, and a suitcase carry is "side": "right" with "implementCount": 1. OMIT it when the objects are NOT identically loaded (40 lb in one hand, 30 in the other): give the true total and the app shows the total alone rather than inventing a split.

kind.description: How the movement is performed. 'dynamic' is ordinary rep work; 'hold' is an isometric; 'carry' is a loaded walk; 'explosive' is an Olympic-style lift judged on peak velocity with no tempo. This says what the movement IS, not how a set of it is measured — whether a set runs on reps or on the clock comes from the set's own reps / duration_s. Omitted: the app uses its built-in definition if the id is one it ships, otherwise guesses from the id, which matches word fragments and gets ordinary names wrong. Declaring it always wins, and any disagreement is flagged at the import gate.

reps.description: Rep count for dynamic sets. Provide exactly one of reps / duration_s.

duration_s.description: Hold/carry duration in seconds for timed sets (plank, farmer's walk). Provide exactly one of reps / duration_s.

load_kg.description: Load in kilograms. Provide at most one of load_kg / load_lb; omit both for bodyweight. May be negative on a bodyweight exercise (see bodyweight): a band or assist machine subtracts from body weight. Always the TOTAL across everything held, including when the exercise declares "implementCount": 2 — write 80 for a pair of 40 lb dumbbells, not 40.

load_lb.description: Load in pounds; converted to kg on import. Provide at most one of load_kg / load_lb; omit both for bodyweight. May be negative on a bodyweight exercise (see bodyweight): a band or assist machine subtracts from body weight. Always the TOTAL across everything held, including when the exercise declares "implementCount": 2 — write 80 for a pair of 40 lb dumbbells, not 40.

side.description: For unilateral exercises (side plank, suitcase carry, single-leg RDL): which side this set trains. Emit one set per side.

note.description: Commentary for THIS SET alone (the exercise-level 'notes' applies to all of its sets). E.g. 'closer to the plate, higher ROM'.

tempo.description: Four-digit tempo. The digits are POSITIONAL: digit 1 is the DOWN stroke, digit 2 the pause at the bottom, digit 3 the UP stroke, digit 4 the pause at the top. Which of the strokes is the eccentric follows from the exercise's 'concentric' direction, not from the digit order. 'X' in digit 3 means explosive. Dash form ('4-0-1-0') is accepted.
